title: Autonomous Units for Disruption
equation: New-Unit Survival = Resource Independence × Metric Independence × Cultural Distance
hook: Your new idea will die if you judge it by the same numbers as your main business.
statement: Protect new, disruptive projects by running them separately from your core business and its rules.
explainer: The habits that make your main business work, like margin targets and approval chains, will choke something new before it can prove itself. Give it room to grow on its own terms.
sop: Pick the one new project that could change your business.
Set it up as its own unit with its own budget.
Give it success metrics separate from the core business.
Let it make its own decisions.
Decide later whether to fold it back in.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Resource Independence 7, Metric Independence 8, Cultural Distance 6. 7 × 8 × 6 = 336 out of 1,000. Higher means the new thing can grow long enough to prove itself. Lower means the parent company will strangle it.
question: Write down the metric your newest project is judged on, and whether it can actually win on it.
closing_statement: Protect what's new from what already works.
caption:
Principle Nº 281: Autonomous Units for Disruption

Your new idea will die if you judge it by the same numbers as your main business.

Protect new, disruptive projects by running them separately from your core business and its rules.
